name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.142.0 — specs/20260910/05: exclusion rows are derived, never hand-typed — ledger derive turns discovery non-goals, no-answered invented rows, and not-needed note withdrawals into exclusion rows; the client confirms them one button each on a journey's last screen before --mark approved will run; --mark roadmap-written refuses any confirmed exclusion missing from the roadmap overview's Parking lot; and --mark approved writes design/mocks/exclusions.md, a dated file a statement of work can cite. 7.141.0 — The escape command's prevention-note step no longer prescribes the escape row's own id as a Gotchas entry's owner citation. That id embeds a timestamp, and the same sentence bans dates in exactly that section, so every entry written to the old instruction was classed as date narration and reddened the repo-wide narration scan. The step now prescribes the spec path the defect escaped plus the spec that fixes it, and says outright that the row id is never the citation. 7.140.0 — The client player's own chrome is now English-only: the two-language STRINGS table and the lang role are retired from lib/walk-page.js and design-atlas.js's clientRoute, closing an escaped defect where the page declared <html lang="en"> while rendering Japanese chrome. Every save on the player now acts only on the server's answer — a mark hides, the open count drops, a note clears or a reached label counts only once the server responds ok, and any refusal or network failure leaves the page unchanged and reports it in a new [data-wk="msg"] status slot instead of guessing ahead of the network. POST /client/__walk/confirm independently refuses with 409 while any question anchored to the journey's screens is unanswered, so a stale tab or a failed player script can no longer record a client sign-off over an open question.
